summary.one_liner: DeepSeek-VL2 is a family of open-weight Mixture-of-Experts vision-language models (Tiny, Small, and base) for image understanding tasks such as visual question answering, OCR, document/chart understanding, and visual grounding.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes three variants with 1.0B, 2.8B, and 4.5B activated parameters (DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny, -Small, and -Base as named in the text). Models are downloadable from Hugging Face with a 4096 sequence length. Quick-start code loads the model via transformers with trust_remote_code and runs single-image, multi-image, and interleaved image-text chat, including visual grounding that returns bounding box coordinates. An incremental prefilling option is shown to reduce GPU memory use for the Small model, and a Gradio web demo and inference script are provided. The README points to vLLM, SGLang, and LMDeploy as options for production deployment, but does not provide them.
use_cases: OCR and text extraction from images
multi-image comparison and interleaved image-text chat
running a local multimodal chat demo
how_to_run: Load model with DeepseekVLV2Processor.from_pretrained and AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_path, trust_remote_code=True), then move to GPU in bfloat16
notable: Mixture-of-Experts vision-language models with 1.0B, 2.8B, and 4.5B activated parameters across three sizes
Visual grounding that outputs bounding box coordinates for referenced objects
Incremental prefilling lets the Small model run within 40GB GPU memory
Supports multi-image and interleaved image-text conversations
Code under MIT License with models under the DeepSeek Model License, which the README says allows commercial use
caveats: The README says about 80GB GPU memory is needed for the Small model, and more for the base model, unless incremental prefilling is used
The bundled Gradio demo is described as a basic implementation without deployment optimizations and may be slow
Model use is subject to the separate DeepSeek Model License
